items.title: Unifor opens negotiations with General Motors
items.summary: Unifor has officially begun contract negotiations with General Motors on behalf of over 4,600 members across Ontario, aiming to secure a new agreement by August 21. Following a pattern agreement established with Ford, the union seeks to ensure job certainty for its members, particularly given that 30% are currently on layoff. Negotiations will focus on company operations and the future of GM auto jobs in Canada.

items.title: Exxon Mobil Corp Stock (XOM) Moved Up by 3.16% on Aug 10: Drivers Behind the Movement
items.summary: Exxon Mobil Corp (XOM) shares rose by 3.16% on August 10, driven by a surge in global crude oil prices due to geopolitical tensions and stronger-than-expected energy demand. The company's operational excellence, including successful integration of Permian Basin assets, and a broader market rotation into energy stocks also contributed to the positive movement. Furthermore, its advancements in low-carbon solutions are beginning to attract ESG-conscious investors.

items.title: Clorox Inflation Pressures Exceed $200M in 2026 | Supply Chain Impact - News and Statistics
items.summary: Clorox anticipates over $200 million in inflationary pressures for 2026, driven by rising energy, commodity, and logistics costs, partly due to shipment disruptions from the Iran war. This figure doubles the company's historical range for cost increases, prompting price hikes on products like Glad trash bags to mitigate the impact on gross margins, which are projected to be around 42% for the current fiscal year. The company expects these inflationary pressures to persist and become more pronounced throughout the year.

items.title: Pentagon Urges Boeing (NYSE: BA), Lockheed (NYSE: LMT) And RTX (NYSE: RTX) To Fast-Track Weapons Output Amid Iran War Strain
items.summary: The Pentagon has officially requested major U.S. defense contractors, including Boeing, Lockheed Martin, and RTX Corp, to expedite the production and delivery of crucial weapons systems. This urgent appeal comes as military stockpiles are strained by the ongoing conflict with Iran. The Department of Defense is particularly focused on accelerating the output of surveillance equipment, air-defense sensors, and missile systems, and has asked contractors to submit plans by late August detailing how they will meet increased demand.

items.title: Clorox expects $200M inflation hit, supply chain costs a factor
items.summary: Clorox anticipates a significant inflation impact of over $200 million this year, primarily driven by rising energy, commodity, and supplier costs, alongside increased trucking, ocean freight, and logistics expenses. The company plans to implement price increases on some products, including Glad trash bags, to offset these pressures, which are proving more persistent than initially expected. Clorox's gross margin for the current fiscal year is projected to be around 42%, a slight decrease from the previous year, reflecting these inflationary challenges.

items.title: Arm Holdings PLC Stock (ARM) Moved Down by 4.64% on Aug 10: What Investors Need To Know
items.summary: Arm Holdings PLC (ARM) stock decreased by 4.64% on August 10th, driven by sector-wide profit-taking, concerns over cooling AI investments, and the negative impact of higher interest rate expectations on its long-term valuation. Geopolitical tensions and regulatory risks in the Asia-Pacific region further suppressed investor confidence. The company's high valuation and sensitivity to macroeconomic factors are making it vulnerable to market volatility.

items.title: Helios Technologies earnings loom as electrification bets tested
items.summary: Helios Technologies is set to report second-quarter earnings, with analysts expecting $0.80 per share on revenue of $230.78 million. Investors will be focused on the company's progress in shifting towards electrified hydraulic systems and its ability to sustain margins amid inflation and product mix shifts. The stock has seen a recent pullback despite strong year-to-date performance, making the upcoming earnings report crucial for evaluating its future momentum and strategic direction.

items.title: Bristol Myers Squibb Advances U.S. Manufacturing Investment with New $2.3 Billion Campus in Houston, Texas
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb announced a $2.3 billion investment to build a new, state-of-the-art multi-modal manufacturing campus in Houston, Texas. This facility will create nearly 500 skilled jobs and is part of BMS's $40 billion commitment to U.S. investment, aiming to accelerate the delivery of next-generation medicines. The modular and multi-modal design allows for manufacturing various types of medicines and adapting to future needs, strengthening American biopharmaceutical leadership and supply chain resilience.
